message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
**This ECG appears abnormal, with a regular rhythm around 100–105 beats/min and a likely left anterior fascicular block.** My reading from the image is preliminary.

- **Rhythm:** Likely sinus rhythm—small P waves appear to precede each beat.
- **Conduction:** The QRS complexes appear narrow. Marked left axis deviation and the pattern in the limb leads suggest **left anterior fascicular block**, a delay in one branch of the heart’s electrical conduction system. [Reference](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/specific-cardiac-arrhythmias/bundle-branch-block-and-fascicular-block)
- **Chest leads:** There is poor R-wave progression, with predominantly downward complexes through V4. This can occur with lead placement, conduction changes, or previous anterior heart damage; this image alone cannot establish the cause.
- **ST/T changes:** There are mild anterior ST changes, and some baseline movement makes assessment harder. I don’t see a definite classic acute ST-elevation heart attack pattern, but **this ECG cannot rule out a heart attack**. Symptoms, comparison with an earlier ECG, and sometimes serial ECGs and troponin blood tests are needed. [Reference](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/coronary-artery-disease/acute-myocardial-infarction-mi)

**If you currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating, or fainting, seek emergency care now.** Otherwise, arrange clinician review and comparison with any previous ECG.

How old is the person, why was the ECG taken, and were there any symptoms?
